name: Insurance claim intake triage
description: A first notice of loss comes in; route it to the desk that should own it.

ask.instructions: Which line of coverage does this claim fall under?

criteria.auto: A vehicle accident, vehicle damage or a stolen vehicle.
criteria.property: Damage to a home or building or its contents: fire, water, wind, hail, theft from the property.
criteria.workers_comp: An employee hurt or made ill while working.
criteria.liability: Someone else says the insured caused them injury or damage, like a slip and fall at the insured's premises.

ask.instructions: Was anyone hurt in the accident?

criteria.true: A driver, passenger or pedestrian was injured, treated or complained of pain.
criteria.false: No one was hurt; vehicle damage only.

ask.instructions: How serious is the worst injury?
criteria: Minor: soreness, no treatment or a single check-up.
Moderate: ER visit, doctor or physical therapy.
Severe: hospitalized, surgery, broken bones or a death.

ask.instructions: Does the auto claim show fraud red flags?

criteria.true: Red flags: a brand-new policy, keys left in the car, no police report, pressure for a quick cash settlement, an inconsistent story or late reporting.
criteria.false: An ordinary, consistent account with nothing unusual.

ask.instructions: How badly is the vehicle damaged?
criteria: Cosmetic: scratches, dents, a cracked bumper.
Not drivable, totaled, burned or stolen.

ask.instructions: Is someone else responsible for the loss, such as another driver, a contractor, a manufacturer or a neighbor?

criteria.true: Another party caused it, for example rear-ended, ran a light, faulty work or a defective product.
criteria.false: No one else is clearly to blame.

ask.instructions: Was the damage caused by a named storm, wildfire, flood or other widespread disaster?

criteria.true: A hurricane, tornado outbreak, wildfire, regional flood or similar event hitting many homes.
criteria.false: A local, one-off event at this property.

criteria.water: Water: burst pipe, leak, appliance overflow.
criteria.weather: Wind, hail, lightning or a fallen tree (not a widespread disaster).

ask.instructions: Does the theft claim show fraud red flags?

criteria.true: Red flags: no police report, a recently bought policy or added coverage, unusually expensive items without receipts, or a vague story.
criteria.false: A police report was filed and the account is ordinary.

ask.instructions: Is the home unlivable, so the family needs somewhere else to stay?

criteria.true: The household is displaced: staying in a hotel or with relatives, no power, water or safe structure.

ask.instructions: Roughly how large is the loss?
How serious is the work injury?
criteria: First aid only, back at work.
Doctor visits, therapy or some days off work.
Surgery, hospitalization, permanent injury or a death.

ask.instructions: Is there reason to doubt the injury happened at work as described?

criteria.true: Reported late, first mentioned on a Monday, no witnesses, a story that changes, or a recent firing or layoff notice.
criteria.false: Reported right away with witnesses or a clear account.

ask.instructions: Is a lawyer involved, or is there a lawsuit or demand letter?

criteria.true: An attorney, a demand letter, a lawsuit or a threat to sue is mentioned.
criteria.false: No lawyer or legal action is mentioned.

fast_track.label: Fast track
fast_track.say: Simple and clear: pay within 48 hours.

subrogation.label: Pay + recover
subrogation.say: Pay the insured, then recover from the party at fault.

adjuster.label: Desk adjuster
adjuster.say: Standard review by a desk adjuster.

total_loss.label: Total-loss desk
total_loss.say: Value the vehicle and settle as a total loss.

urgent_field.label: Field adjuster today
urgent_field.say: Family displaced: send a field adjuster and arrange temporary housing.

cat_team.label: Catastrophe team
cat_team.say: Part of a disaster: route to the CAT response team.

nurse.label: Nurse case manager
nurse.say: Serious injury: assign a nurse case manager and set a large reserve.

large_loss.label: Large-loss unit
large_loss.say: High severity: senior adjuster and large-loss reserve.

siu.label: Fraud investigation
siu.say: Red flags: refer to the Special Investigations Unit before paying.

legal.label: Defense counsel
legal.say: Lawyer involved: assign litigation handling and defense counsel.

examples.title: Rear-ended at a red light
examples.text: Insured was stopped at a red light on Westheimer when a pickup rear-ended her. Bumper and trunk are damaged but the car is drivable. Nobody was hurt. Police report filed and the other driver was cited.

examples.title: Stolen car, new policy
examples.text: Insured reports his 2019 Camry was stolen from his driveway last night. He bought the policy three weeks ago and says he left the keys inside. He is asking for a quick cash settlement.

examples.title: Broken leg, in surgery
examples.text: Two-car collision at an intersection. Our driver was taken by ambulance with a broken leg and is in surgery now.

examples.title: Kitchen fire, family displaced
examples.text: Kitchen fire started at the stove. Smoke damage throughout the first floor. The family of four is staying at a hotel; the house is not livable.

examples.title: Burst pipe, $2,800
examples.text: Pipe burst under the bathroom sink and damaged the vanity and some flooring. A plumber already fixed it; the repair estimate is $2,800.

examples.title: Hurricane roof damage
examples.text: Hurricane Delta tore part of the roof off and water is coming into the attic. The whole neighborhood has been without power since Tuesday.

examples.title: Back injury reported late
examples.text: Warehouse employee says he slipped on a wet floor last Friday but first reported it this Monday morning. No witnesses. He has lower back pain and wants to see a chiropractor.

examples.title: Fall with a lawyer's letter
examples.text: A customer slipped on ice in our store parking lot and broke her wrist. We have received a letter from her attorney demanding $75,000.
